+package dev.pathland.docs
+
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+import java.nio.file.Files
+import java.nio.file.Path
+import java.util.Locale
+
+/** The docs content set: pages, navigation, TOC and prev/next resolution. */
+class DocsRepository(
+    pages: List<DocsPage>,
+    private val routePrefix: String = "/docs",
+) {
+    val pages: List<DocsPage> = pages
+        .filterNot { it.draft }
+        .sortedWith(compareBy<DocsPage>({ it.section ?: "" }, { it.order }, { it.title }))
+
+    private val byRoute: Map<String, DocsPage> = buildMap {
+        for (page in this@DocsRepository.pages) {
+            require(!containsKey(page.route)) { "duplicate docs route: ${page.route}" }
+            put(page.route, page)
+        }
+    }
+
+    private val bySource: Map<String, DocsPage> =
+        this.pages.associateBy { normalizeSource(it.sourcePath) }
+
+    init {
+        require(this.pages.isNotEmpty()) { "docs repository is empty" }
+    }
+
+    fun page(route: String): DocsPage? = byRoute[normalize(route)]
+
+    fun sections(): List<DocsSection> =
+        pages.groupBy { it.section }.map { (section, pages) -> DocsSection(section, pages) }
+
+    fun toc(page: DocsPage): List<MarkdownHeading> = MarkdownHeadings.extract(page.markdown)
+
+    fun previous(page: DocsPage): DocsPage? {
+        val index = pages.indexOfFirst { it.route == page.route }
+        return if (index > 0) pages[index - 1] else null
+    }
+
+    fun next(page: DocsPage): DocsPage? {
+        val index = pages.indexOfFirst { it.route == page.route }
+        return if (index >= 0 && index + 1 < pages.size) pages[index + 1] else null
+    }
+
+    fun routes(): List<String> = pages.map { it.route }
+
+    /**
+     * Resolve a Markdown link from [page]: relative `.md` targets become routes,
+     * while absolute URLs, fragments, and non-Markdown paths are left alone.
+     */
+    fun resolveLink(page: DocsPage, href: String): String {
+        val trimmed = href.trim()
+        if (trimmed.isEmpty() || trimmed.startsWith("#") || trimmed.startsWith("/") ||
+            trimmed.startsWith("http://") || trimmed.startsWith("https://") ||
+            trimmed.startsWith("mailto:") || trimmed.startsWith("tel:")
+        ) {
+            return href
+        }
+        val cut = listOf(trimmed.indexOf('#'), trimmed.indexOf('?'))
+            .filter { it >= 0 }.minOrNull() ?: trimmed.length
+        val path = trimmed.substring(0, cut)
+        val suffix = trimmed.substring(cut)
+        if (!path.endsWith(".md") && !path.endsWith(".markdown")) return href
+        val baseDir = normalizeSource(page.sourcePath).substringBeforeLast('/', "")
+        val resolved = normalizePath(if (baseDir.isEmpty()) path else "$baseDir/$path")
+        val target = bySource[resolved] ?: bySource[resolved.removePrefix("docs/")]
+        return (target?.route ?: href) + suffix
+    }
+
+    private fun normalize(route: String): String {
+        val path = route.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#')
+        val withSlash = if (path.startsWith('/')) path else "/$path"
+        return if (withSlash.length > 1) withSlash.trimEnd('/') else withSlash
+    }
+
+    private fun normalizeSource(path: String): String =
+        path.replace('\\', '/').removePrefix("./").trimStart('/')
+
+    private fun normalizePath(path: String): String {
+        val parts = ArrayList<String>()
+        for (segment in path.replace('\\', '/').split('/')) {
+            when (segment) {
+                "", "." -> continue
+                ".." -> if (parts.isNotEmpty()) parts.removeAt(parts.lastIndex)
+                else -> parts.add(segment)
+            }
+        }
+        return parts.joinToString("/")
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        /** Read the `.md` resources named by a classpath index (one path per line). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        @JvmOverloads
+        fun fromResources(
+            indexResource: String = "META-INF/pathland-docs.index",
+            routePrefix: String = "/docs",
+            classLoader: ClassLoader = Thread.currentThread().contextClassLoader
+                ?: DocsRepository::class.java.classLoader,
+        ): DocsRepository {
+            val index = classLoader.getResourceAsStream(indexResource)
+                ?: error("missing docs index resource: $indexResource")
+            val paths = index.bufferedReader(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).useLines { lines ->
+                lines.map { it.trim() }
+                    .filter { it.isNotEmpty() && !it.startsWith("#") }
+                    .toList()
+            }
+            val pages = paths.map { path ->
+                val stream = classLoader.getResourceAsStream(path)
+                    ?: error("missing docs resource: $path")
+                val raw = stream.bufferedReader(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).use { it.readText() }
+                DocsPage.fromMarkdown(path, raw, routePrefix)
+            }
+            return DocsRepository(pages, routePrefix)
+        }
+
+        /** Read a filesystem directory (dev mode / tests). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        @JvmOverloads
+        fun fromDirectory(
+            directory: Path,
+            routePrefix: String = "/docs",
+        ): DocsRepository {
+            require(Files.isDirectory(directory)) { "docs directory not found: $directory" }
+            val pages = Files.walk(directory).use { paths ->
+                paths.filter { Files.isRegularFile(it) && it.fileName.toString().endsWith(".md") }
+                    .sorted()
+                    .map { file ->
+                        val relative = directory.relativize(file).toString().replace('\\', '/')
+                        DocsPage.fromMarkdown(
+                            sourcePath = relative,
+                            raw = Files.readString(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
+                            routePrefix = routePrefix,
+                        )
+                    }
+                    .toList()
+            }
+            return DocsRepository(pages, routePrefix)
+        }
+
+        /** Build a repository from explicit Markdown strings (tests / small sites). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        @JvmOverloads
+        fun fromMarkdown(
+            entries: Map<String, String>,
+            routePrefix: String = "/docs",
+        ): DocsRepository = DocsRepository(
+            entries.map { (path, raw) -> DocsPage.fromMarkdown(path, raw, routePrefix) },
+            routePrefix,
+        )
+    }
+}
+
+/** A heading extracted for a table of contents. */
+data class MarkdownHeading(
+    val level: Int,
+    val id: String,
+    val text: String,
+)
+
+/** Heading extraction + slugging (the same rules the block renderer uses). */
+object MarkdownHeadings {
+    private val ATX = Regex("^\\s{0,3}(#{1,6})\\s+(.*?)\\s*#*\\s*$")
+
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun extract(markdown: String): List<MarkdownHeading> {
+        val headings = ArrayList<MarkdownHeading>()
+        val slugger = Slugger()
+        var fence = false
+        for (line in markdown.lineSequence()) {
+            val trimmed = line.trimStart()
+            if (trimmed.startsWith("```") || trimmed.startsWith("~~~")) {
+                fence = !fence
+                continue
+            }
+            if (fence) continue
+            val match = ATX.matchEntire(line) ?: continue
+            val level = match.groupValues[1].length
+            val text = match.groupValues[2].trim()
+            if (text.isEmpty()) continue
+            headings.add(MarkdownHeading(level, slugger.slug(plain(text)), plain(text)))
+        }
+        return headings
+    }
+
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun plain(inline: String): String =
+        inline.replace(Regex("!?\\[([^\\]]*)]\\([^)]*\\)"), "$1")
+            .replace(Regex("[*_`~]"), "")
+            .replace(Regex("\\\\([\\\\`*_{}\\[\\]()#+.!~-])"), "$1")
+            .trim()
+}
+
+/** Unique, GitHub-style heading ids (`intro`, `intro-1`, …). */
+class Slugger {
+    private val seen = HashMap<String, Int>()
+
+    fun slug(text: String): String {
+        val base = MarkdownHeadings.plain(text)
+            .lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+            .replace(Regex("[^a-z0-9\\s-]"), "")
+            .trim()
+            .replace(Regex("\\s+"), "-")
+            .trim('-')
+            .ifEmpty { "section" }
+        val count = seen[base] ?: 0
+        seen[base] = count + 1
+        return if (count == 0) base else "$base-$count"
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.docs
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.View
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Categories
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Components
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Properties
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.FrameOpcodeSink
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.ProtocolFrame
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+
+class MarkdownViewTest {
+
+    private fun mount(root: View): ProtocolFrame {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        Emitter(sink).mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        return sink.frame()
+    }
+
+    private fun created(frame: ProtocolFrame): List<Int> = frame.opcodes()
+        .filter { it.category() == Categories.TREE && it.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE }
+        .map { it.b() and 0xFFFF }
+
+    private fun props(frame: ProtocolFrame): List<Int> = frame.opcodes()
+        .filter { it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY }
+        .map { it.b() and 0xFFFF }
+
+    private fun texts(frame: ProtocolFrame): List<String> = frame.opcodes()
+        .filter { it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT }
+        .map { frame.stringAt(it.b()) }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rendersHeadingWithAnchorAndParagraph() {
+        val frame = mount(Markdown("# Getting started\n\nHello **world**."))
+        assertTrue(Components.TEXT in created(frame))
+        assertTrue(Properties.ANCHOR in props(frame), "heading carries an anchor: ${props(frame)}")
+        assertTrue(texts(frame).contains("Getting started"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rendersListsAndImages() {
+        val frame = mount(
+            Markdown(
+                """
+                - one
+                - two
+
+                ![shot](/docs-assets/shot.png)
+                """.trimIndent(),
+            ),
+        )
+        assertTrue(Components.HSTACK in created(frame), "list rows are HStacks")
+        assertTrue(Components.IMAGE in created(frame), "block image is an IMAGE")
+        assertEquals(2, texts(frame).count { it == "•" })
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rendersCodeBlockWithPreservedWhitespace() {
+        val frame = mount(Markdown("```kotlin\nfun main() {\n    println(\"hi\")\n}\n```"))
+        assertTrue(Components.SCROLLVIEW in created(frame))
+        assertTrue(Properties.WHITE_SPACE in props(frame), "code block sets WHITE_SPACE")
+        assertTrue(texts(frame).any { it.contains("    println") })
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rendersGfmTable() {
+        val frame = mount(
+            Markdown(
+                """
+                | A | B |
+                |---|---|
+                | 1 | 2 |
+                """.trimIndent(),
+            ),
+        )
+        assertTrue(Components.GRID in created(frame), "table is a GRID")
+        assertTrue(texts(frame).containsAll(listOf("A", "B", "1", "2")))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun parsesFrontMatterAndRoutes() {
+        val page = DocsPage.fromMarkdown(
+            "content/docs/guides/install.md",
+            """
+            ---
+            title: Install
+            description: How to install it.
+            section: Guides
+            order: 7
+            ---
+
+            # Ignored heading
+            Body.
+            """.trimIndent(),
+        )
+        assertEquals("Install", page.title)
+        assertEquals("/docs/guides/install", page.route)
+        assertEquals("Guides", page.section)
+        assertEquals(7, page.order)
+        assertEquals("How to install it.", page.description)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun resolvesRelativeMarkdownLinksToRoutes() {
+        val repo = DocsRepository.fromMarkdown(
+            mapOf(
+                "docs/index.md" to "# Home\n",
+                "docs/guides/install.md" to "# Install\n",
+                "docs/guides/config.md" to "# Config\n",
+            ),
+        )
+        val install = repo.page("/docs/guides/install")!!
+        assertEquals("/docs/guides/config", repo.resolveLink(install, "config.md"))
+        assertEquals("/docs/guides/config#advanced", repo.resolveLink(install, "config.md#advanced"))
+        assertEquals("https://example.com", repo.resolveLink(install, "https://example.com"))
+        assertEquals("#local", repo.resolveLink(install, "#local"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun sluggerDeduplicatesHeadings() {
+        val headings = MarkdownHeadings.extract("# Intro\n\n## Intro\n\n## Hello, world!")
+        assertEquals(listOf("intro", "intro-1", "hello-world"), headings.map { it.id })
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rawHtmlStaysLiteral() {
+        val frame = mount(Markdown("<script>alert(1)</script>"))
+        assertTrue(texts(frame).any { it.contains("<script>") })
+    }
+}

+# pathland-docs — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 6, 2026
+
+The reusable Kotlin docs kit: CommonMark/GFM block parsing into Pathland views,
+code blocks, tables, a `.md` resource repository, and a docs page shell. It emits
+**views**, never HTML — the renderers remain the only HTML producers.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **Block Markdown** (`Markdown(...)`, CommonMark + GFM tables/strikethrough):
+  headings (with `ANCHOR` ids), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/nested lists, task
+  list markers, fenced/indented code blocks, block quotes, thematic breaks,
+  GFM tables, block images, inline links, and raw-HTML-as-literal-text.
+- **Inline rendering** into `AttributedString` (bold/italic/code/strikethrough/
+  links; images become alt text), with a `linkResolver` hook and `imageBase`
+  prefix.
+- **`CodeBlock`**: monospace, `WHITE_SPACE = PRE`, optional language label,
+  padding/background/border, horizontal scroll. **No syntax highlighting** (see
+  issue #188; deferred deliberately).
+- **Tables**: `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling and per-cell alignment.
+  Visual only — semantic table roles are deferred with the protocol work.
+- **TOC**: `MarkdownHeadings.extract` + `Slugger` (duplicate-safe ids).
+- **Link resolution**: `DocsRepository.resolveLink` maps relative `.md` targets
+  (including fragments/queries) to the target page's route; absolute URLs and
+  fragments pass through.
+- **`DocsPage.fromMarkdown`**: flat front matter (`title`, `description`,
+  `section`, `order`, `route`, `draft`, `updated`, `image`), route derivation,
+  and a `DocsRepository` that loads an index + classpath resources or a
+  filesystem directory.
+- **`DocsLayout`**: header, sidebar, content, TOC, prev/next, per-page
+  `windowMetadata`.
+- **Tests**: `MarkdownViewTest` covers headings/anchors, lists/images, code
+  whitespace, GFM tables, front matter/routes, slug dedupe, and raw HTML.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- Syntax highlighting (issue #188).
+- Semantic table roles (deferred; tables are visual grids for now).
+- Inline images inside a paragraph (rendered as alt text; block images only).
+- Footnotes, GFM alerts/admonitions, and autolinks beyond CommonMark.
+- A build-time docs index generator (the demo ships a hand-maintained
+  `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`; `DocsRepository.fromDirectory` covers dev/tests).

 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
 their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
 `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
 `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
 capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
 - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
   Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
   application config (including
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
 
-- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
+- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. The sitemap includes the app root plus every route declared by `PathlandApp.sitemapRoutes()` (e.g. docs pages).
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL
   from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
 - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
   Same stateless rule as the root socket.
 - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
   Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
   **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
 - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
 - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
   `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
   mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.
 - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
 - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.
 - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
 - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
 - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
   a Java CDI bean can mount them.
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @ApplicationScoped
 public class MyApp {
     @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
 Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
 spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
 and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
 `GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
 (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
 covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
 sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
 probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
 and is never closed by the peer.
 `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
 check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`
 (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR `<link>`, the immutable `text/css`
 response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.

 # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
 port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
 self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
 one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
 is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
 library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
   `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
   `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
   self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
   former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
 - **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
   committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
   fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
   client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
 - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root,
   meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter
   cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
   Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The
   document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's
   `document_meta.document.html` fixture.
+- **Docs primitives**: `WHITE_SPACE` renders `white-space:normal|nowrap|pre|pre-wrap`; `ANCHOR` (STRING) becomes the element `id` attribute. Mirrored by the Rust renderer + DOM client.
 - **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
   (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
   attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
   surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
   size-that-fits snapshots.
 - **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
   the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
   default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
   `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
   `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
 - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
   with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
 - **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
   canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
   so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
 - **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
   `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
   external/webfont requests.
 - The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
   truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
   and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
 DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
 run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

 # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
   lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
   `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
   correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
   configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
   config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
-- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
+- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. The sitemap includes the app root plus every route declared by `PathlandApp.sitemapRoutes()` (e.g. docs pages).
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
   URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.

+    /** Preserve newlines/indentation and do not wrap (code blocks). */

 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the

 signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
 interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.

-  `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.

+  `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.

+  same parser the docs kit uses) in a restricted inline-only mode: only
+  paragraph blocks are accepted, so headings/lists/fences stay literal in a
+  text view. The existing Rust/JVM inline output contract is preserved by the
+  `MarkdownTest` parity suite. Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path;
+  rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive
+  `Text(Signal<String>)` parses on change.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
   `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
   **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled
   `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them
   against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are
   bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). A declared `opcodeCount` that overflows
   `Int` arithmetic now throws instead of triggering an OOM allocation.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
   `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
   protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
   `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
   public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
   Java source is generated.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
   protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
   the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
+- **Docs primitives**: `.whiteSpace(WhiteSpace.NORMAL|NO_WRAP|PRE|PRE_WRAP)` /
+  `.preserveWhitespace(wrap = false)` and `.anchor(id)` (a stable HTML/Native
+  anchor for deep links and TOCs).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module: `core`/`engine`/`dsl` are logical
   subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
   (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
   them into separate artifacts would require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on this module. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 # pathland-core — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **protocol core**: 16-byte opcode, SPSC ring buffers (both directions),
 bump arenas (both directions), memory layout, typed events, and the golden
 conformance vectors. The protocol contract is defined in `spec/`; this file
 tracks what this crate implements.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window/surface metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` 0x08, draft): an extensible field family (`TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCALE`) for the hosting window/surface, plus the shared no_std `WindowMeta` decoder helper. Spec + conformance vectors 44–45.
 
 - **Component types** (`constants.rs::component_type`): the full grouped map —
   `TEXT 0x01, IMAGE 0x02, COLOR 0x03, SHAPE 0x04, DIVIDER 0x05, SPACER 0x06,
   PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07, GAUGE 0x08, VIDEO 0x0A, ICON 0x0B, VSTACK 0x10, HSTACK 0x11, ZSTACK 0x12, GRID
 0x13, SCROLLVIEW 0x14, LAZY_VGRID 0x15, LAZY_HGRID 0x16, LAZY_VSTACK 0x1B,
    LAZY_HSTACK 0x1C, GRID_ROW 0x1D, PROXY_VIEW 0x1E, BUTTON 0x20, TEXT_FIELD 0x21, TEXT_EDITOR 0x22, TOGGLE
    0x24, SLIDER 0x25, STEPPER 0x26, DATE_PICKER 0x27, PICKER 0x28, MENU 0x29,
    COLOR_PICKER 0x2A, MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30, COMMENT 0x7F`. (`0x09` formerly
    `AUDIO` is freed — audio has no view; spec/MEDIA.md.)
 - **Media kit** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (`0x30`, **non-visual**,
   layout-transparent) owns the resource + transport; a `VIDEO` (`0x0A`) surface
   references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (`0x103A`). Transport properties
   `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035), `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036), `MEDIA_VOLUME` (0x1037),
   `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D),
   `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E); the `MEDIA_*` events target the **controller** id and add
   `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` (0x14). Covered by conformance vectors 39–41.
 - **`PROXY_VIEW`** (`0x1E`) — a container whose child subtree is served by another
   Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md); the id is the only wire-visible part of the
   proxy contract (the origin subtree's nodes are ordinary opcodes with
   **id-remapped** node ids). Covered by conformance vector 38.
 - **`GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`** (`0x001E`/`0x001F`, F32) track-count properties
   for grids (positive = count, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit; never a pixel box),
   **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track specs (takes precedence over the
   counts), and the **`GRID_ROW`** (`0x1D`) component (a grid child whose children
   are one row's cells) — all covered by conformance vectors (34–36).
 - **`ALIGNMENT` (0x0002) is a 2D position code (0–8)**: `0` topLeading, `1`
   center, `2` bottomTrailing, `3` topCenter, `4` bottomCenter, `5` centerLeading,
   `6` centerTrailing, `7` topTrailing, `8` bottomLeading. Stacks read one axis
   (`VSTACK`→horizontal, `HSTACK`→vertical; codes 0/1/2 backward-compatible);
   `ZSTACK`/grids read both. Position-only — stretching is a child's `FILL`
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, never an alignment (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). Covered by
   conformance vector 37 (`ALIGNMENT` topCenter = 3).
 - **Properties** (`property_id`): the full `spec/MODIFIERS.md` catalog —
   stack/text/styling/semantic IDs plus every draft modifier (`SHAPE_KIND`,
   layout `OFFSET`/`POSITION`/frame bounds/`FIXED_SIZE`/`LAYOUT_PRIORITY`/
   `ASPECT_RATIO`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`, text-format
   `FONT_STYLE`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`FONT_WIDTH`/`KERNING`/`TRACKING`/
   `BASELINE_OFFSET`/`LINE_SPACING`/`TEXT_CASE`/`UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
   effects `SHADOW_*`/`BLUR_RADIUS`/`SATURATION`/`CONTRAST`/`BRIGHTNESS`/
   `GRAYSCALE`/`HUE_ROTATION`/`COLOR_MULTIPLY`/`COLOR_INVERT`,
   `ROTATION_DEGREES`/`SCALE`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, control drafts
   `STEP_VALUE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`IS_SECURE`/`PROGRESS`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`/
   `SELECTION`/`COLOR_VALUE`/`DATE_PICKER_MODE`/`PICKER_STYLE`,
   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`, the **asset references** `IMAGE_SOURCE`

Base literals are compiled into literals and never emitted; semantic + component tokens are emitted in four layers (`:root`, platform-dark media, forced-dark/light scheme selectors, and the `--pl-dark-*` forced-dark family). - `design/html/{reset,components}.css` holds the hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` rules. Component rules consume `var(--pl-*)` tokens; no design-relevant literal remains (sizes, radii, border widths, durations, z-index, focus rings, opacities). - `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs` provide build/watch/validation. `check` verifies Tier-1 catalog coverage, layer/reference direction, dark/forced-dark declarations, `$extensions.pathland.internal` markings, and that every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by `token_spec::isLengthToken`. - `design/build/base.css` + `base.css.name` (the SHA-256 content hash, e.g. `base-5f86423db422.css`) are synced to `assets/` by `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` (and `--check` fails on drift). `src/css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!`; `builtin_css()` / `builtin_css_name()` expose them and `STYLE` wraps the bundle in `<style>`. - **External stylesheet mode**: `render_document` stays inline (the library default); `render_document_linked(opcodes, strings, root, css_base)` emits `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{css_base}/{name}">` instead. The C ABI adds `pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`, and `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java port + Spring/Quarkus starters expose them and serve the CSS immutable. The `_tailwind_compile` entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`, `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**. Non-JVM hosts that embed the cdylib must refresh it with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` (not just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the shared library). The JVM no longer embeds it; `GoldenConformanceTest` guards the Java port against golden-fixture drift. - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors, strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`). ## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift) The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). The SSR output is the contract both renderers must satisfy. ## Not implemented / gaps - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (spec/LAYOUT.md §content fitting): aligned — it **alone** has no observable effect (the old `nowrap`+`text-overflow:ellipsis` emission is gone, SSR + TS DOM client); under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp the renderer tail- ellipsizes via `line-clamp`. Renderer-owned fidelity: CSS cannot place a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to the tail ellipsis. - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding/content margins, corner radius, opacity, width/height, border width/color, shadow color/x/y/radius). **Parent-path fallback and per-component native control chrome are not implemented in CSS** (see the gaps above). - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**: grids emit `gap` from `SPACING`, equal-`1fr` track templates from the `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/ LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/ `minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, taking precedence over the count), and **per-cell alignment** — each cell is wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell, else the grid `ALIGNMENT` position (default start) — with `justify-items`/ `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`) and renders **only its first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C14 covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. the `gridrow` scenario). - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property). - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact. - **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web. - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — no external/webfont loading, so the rendered document makes no network requests for fonts and works offline. An app can still pick its own typeface via a `font.body.family` `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override (any STRING value, e.g. `"Inter"` if the app hosts it). - Compound token refs cover shadow x/y/radius and border width (the DOM client mirrors them); per-component tokens still style only the component CSS the renderer owns. ## Verified by `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 77 headless render tests (components, properties, composite, event attrs, navigation slot route/transition attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames, inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). The built-in CSS tests assert the generated bundle is embedded (reset, tokens, component rules) and that component rules reference the catalog/metadata tokens; the linked-mode tests assert the hashed `<link>` and that the default render remains inline. `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard. `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check` and `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` validate the design pipeline and the committed bundle.

 /// Emit the token conventions (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`)
 /// from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the pure data + pure functions the
 /// DOM client imports, so the `--pl-*` naming / length rules cannot drift.
 pub fn emit_tokens_core_ts() -> String {
     let mut out = String::new();
     out.push_str(
         "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
          // Canonical design-token conventions from `pathland-render-html::token_spec`\n\
          // (spec/TOKENS.md). Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
     );
     let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
     let list = |items: &[&str]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|s| q(*s)).collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     let pair_list = |items: &[(&str, &str)]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items
             .iter()
             .map(|(a, b)| format!("[{}, {}]", q(*a), q(*b)))
             .collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     writeln!(out, "export const DARK_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::DARK_PREFIX)).unwrap();
     writeln!(out, "export const VAR_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::VAR_PREFIX)).unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX = {};",
         q(token_spec::FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(out, "export const SPACE_FAMILY = {};", q(token_spec::SPACE_FAMILY)).unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_PREFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIXES)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = {};",
         pair_list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_EXACT: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_EXACT)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES)
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "\n/** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` → `-`.\n \
          *  The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the same\n \
          *  variable inside a media query. */\n\
          export function tokenToCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 return VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */\n\
          export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
          \x20 return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The forced-dark variable for a token path (`--pl-dark-<path>`). */\n\
          export function tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 return FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`). */\n\
          export function isLengthToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
          \x20 for (const prefix of LENGTH_PREFIXES) {\n\
          \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix)) return true;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 for (const [prefix, suffix] of LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX) {\n\
          \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix) && path.endsWith(suffix)) return true;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 if (LENGTH_EXACT.includes(path)) return true;\n\
          \x20 return path.startsWith(\"elevation.\") && LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES.some((s) => path.endsWith(s));\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Resolve a `DESIGN_TOKEN` property reference to a CSS expression: the\n\
           *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;\n\
           *  an explicit `dark.` reference uses the forced-dark variable family; every\n\
           *  other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>, unset)`. */\n\
          export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const forcedDark = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
          \x20 const bare = forcedDark ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 if (bare.startsWith(SPACE_FAMILY)) {\n\
          \x20\x20 const rest = bare.slice(SPACE_FAMILY.length);\n\
          \x20\x20 if (rest.length > 0 && !Number.isNaN(Number(rest))) {\n\
          \x20\x20\x20 const base = forcedDark ? \"--pl-dark-space-base\" : \"--pl-space-base\";\n\
          \x20\x20\x20 return `calc(var(${base}) * ${rest})`;\n\
          \x20\x20 }\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 if (forcedDark) {\n\
          \x20\x20 return `var(${tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return `var(${tokenToCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
          }\n",
     );
     out
 }
 
 /// Emit the role→semantic-element conventions (`generated/role-spec.ts`) from
 /// `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — the single source the Rust SSR renderer
 /// and the DOM client share for semantic tags / ARIA fallbacks.
 pub fn emit_role_spec_ts() -> String {
     let mut out = String::new();
     out.push_str(
         "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
          // Canonical ROLE → semantic HTML element mapping from\n\
          // `pathland-render-html::role_spec` (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties).\n\
          // Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
     );
     let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
     let nums = |items: &[u16]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|v| format!("{v:#06x}")).collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const GENERIC_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
         nums(role_spec::GENERIC_COMPONENTS)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
         nums(role_spec::NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS)
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "export interface RoleTag {\n\
          \x20 role: number;\n\
          \x20 tag: string;\n\
          \x20 aria: string;\n\
          }\n\n",
     );
     out.push_str("export const ROLE_TAGS: readonly RoleTag[] = [\n");
     for rt in role_spec::ROLE_TAGS {
         writeln!(out, "  {{ role: {}, tag: {}, aria: {} }},", rt.role, q(rt.tag), q(rt.aria)).unwrap();
     }
     out.push_str("];\n\n");
     let heading_pairs: Vec<String> = role_spec::HEADING_STYLES
         .iter()
         .map(|(style, level)| format!("[{style}, {level}]"))
         .collect();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const HEADING_STYLES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [{}];",
         heading_pairs.join(", ")
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "\n/** The heading level a `TEXT_STYLE` typography implies, or null for the\n \
          *  non-heading styles (Subheadline, Body, Caption, …). */\n\
          export function headingLevel(textStyle: number): number | null {\n\
          \x20 const found = HEADING_STYLES.find(([s]) => s === textStyle);\n\
          \x20 return found ? found[1] : null;\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The heading element tag for a level (1 → `h1` … 5 → `h5`). */\n\
          export function headingTag(level: number): string {\n\
          \x20 return \"h\" + String(level);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** A shell's role behavior (see `pathland-render-html::role_spec`).\n \
           *  Generic `div`/`span` shells may be retagged; native controls convey\n \
           *  their own role; anything else only gets an ARIA attribute. */\n\
          export type ShellKind = \"generic\" | \"native\" | \"other\";\n\n\
          /** The semantic tag a `(shell kind, role)` pair resolves to, or null. */\n\
          export function semanticTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind !== \"generic\") return null;\n\
          \x20 const found = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
          \x20 return found ? found.tag : null;\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The effective tag for a generic TEXT shell: a heading `TEXT_STYLE`\n\
           *  wins (always a heading), then the semantic role (`ROLE_HEADER` → `<h2>`,\n\
           *  `ROLE_PARAGRAPH` → `<p>`, landmarks), else null (→ `<span>`). */\n\
          export function textTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number, textStyle: number | null): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind === \"generic\" && textStyle !== null) {\n\
          \x20\x20 const level = headingLevel(textStyle);\n\
          \x20\x20 if (level !== null) return headingTag(level);\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return semanticTag(kind, role);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The ARIA `role` value to emit for `(shell kind, role)`, or null when\n\
           *  the element already conveys the role (a semantic tag or a native control). */\n\
          export function ariaRole(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind === \"native\") return null;\n\
          \x20 const tagged = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
          \x20 if (tagged) {\n\
          \x20\x20 return kind === \"generic\" ? null : tagged.aria;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return null;\n\
          }\n",
     );
     out
 }
 
 fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
     let consts = constants_ts_path();
     std::fs::write(&consts, emit_constants_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", consts.display());
     let tokens = tokens_core_ts_path();
     if let Some(parent) = tokens.parent() {
         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
     }
     std::fs::write(&tokens, emit_tokens_core_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", tokens.display());
     let roles = role_spec_ts_path();
     if let Some(parent) = roles.parent() {
         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
     }
     std::fs::write(&roles, emit_role_spec_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", roles.display());
     Ok(())
 }
