 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Kotlin with the hand-written
 > **`dev.pathland.view.dsl` DSL** (reusable JVM library, Java 17+); both drive the
 > engine through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a
 > zero-copy shared ring on desktop. Java hosts mount Kotlin views through
 > `PathlandApp`.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Kotlin/JVM `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)

 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base

 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
 design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates

   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.

   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.

 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Kotlin DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Kotlin DSL
 (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - The Java/Kotlin desktop demo (`pathland-desktop-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk`
   as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Kotlin view's
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared view the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Kotlin JVM authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`, in `lib/java/pathland-view-core`)
 
 The **sole JVM authoring surface**. It is the SwiftUI-like DSL shared by desktop,
 Spring Boot, Quarkus, and web apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open Kotlin interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code defines its own views by
   extending `Component` or implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()`; a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later write
   re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound
   to a node stays fine-grained and does not re-run the body. Plain
   `if`/`when`/`for` works; `ForEach` is the reactive list component.
 - **Builders and modifiers**: `VStack(spacing = 8f) { … }`, `Text("hi")`,
   `Button("Save") { … }`, `.padding`, `.frame`, `.fontSize`, `.background`,
   `.buttonStyle(BorderedButtonStyle)`, `.windowMetadata`, navigation intents, and
   the full modifier vocabulary. Styles are Kotlin values
   (`PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`).
 - **Builder scopes**: view blocks take a `PathlandScope` receiver. `PathlandScope`,
   `Navigation.Builder`, and modifier/style `Config` receivers share the
   `@PathlandDsl` marker, so an outer router/config receiver cannot be captured
   implicitly inside a nested view block (compile-time guard only; the
   thread-local `ViewScopes` stack still collects children).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` provides `val count by state(0)` (auto-keyed
   by property name) or `state(0, "key")`, bound to the session's
   `PersistentState` before the first `body()` render — no annotation processor or
   kapt.
 - **Java hosting**: Java Spring Boot/Quarkus apps remain first-class hosts. A
   Java `PathlandApp` bean returns a Kotlin `View`
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`); no Kotlin compiler or authoring DSL is
   needed in the host module. Every reusable Kotlin root exposes a public
   constructor or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factory with Java-friendly types.
 - **Consistency** with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the
   emitter/HTML tests (golden byte layout + round-trips).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.

 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→JVM source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Kotlin DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
 5. If emission behavior changed, run
    `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
 6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
 7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

-title: Architecture
-description: The opcode engine, shared ring, arena, and renderer contract.
-section: Concepts
-order: 20
----
-
-# Architecture
-
-Pathland has four moving parts.
-
-## 1. The application owns the tree
-
-The application builds a retained view tree. Nodes carry properties,
-constraints, text, event listeners, and signal bindings. The application owns
-all business state.
-
-## 2. The engine emits deltas
-
-The engine compares the new tree with the previous snapshot and emits only the
-changes:
-
-```text
-TREE      CREATE_NODE / INSERT_CHILD / REMOVE_CHILD / DELETE_NODE / MOVE_CHILD
-PARAMETER SET_PROPERTY / SET_TEXT / SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT / SET_DESIGN_TOKEN
-META      RESET / ENVIRONMENT / WINDOW_METADATA / RESYNC
-EVENT     POINTER_* / KEY_* / TEXT_CHANGED / NAVIGATE / MEDIA_*
-```
-
-An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.
-
-## 3. The transport is shared memory or a binary batch
-
-Every opcode is 16 bytes:
-
-```text
-[category: u8][command: u8][flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
-```
-
-On desktop, the guest writes into a ring buffer in shared linear memory. Over
-the network, the same opcodes travel in a `PLPL` batch with a string section.
-
-## 4. The renderer maps to native elements
-
-Renderers are stateless with respect to the application:
-
-- HTML → flex containers, spans, buttons, native form controls
-- GTK4 → `GtkBox`, `GtkLabel`, `GtkButton`, …
-- Qt Quick → Row/Column/Text and Qt Quick Controls
-
-Renderers keep only their own rendered output tree — a cache for drawing, hit
-testing, and event routing. They never keep application state.
-
-> The engine describes WHAT the UI is, never WHERE it is. It does not compute
-> layout and does not emit rects.

-# Button
-
-An action trigger with a native button element.
-
-## Overview
-
-Buttons report pointer events through the opcode engine and resolve to a native `<button>` on the web. Use a ButtonStyle for custom visuals, or `.navigate(route)` to make a navigation link.
-
-## Live example
-
-```kotlin live=component-button
-var count by state(0)
-
-VStack(spacing = 8f) {
-    Text("Count: $count")
-    HStack(spacing = 8f) {
-        Button("−") { count -= 1 }
-        Button("+") { count += 1 }
-    }
-}
-```
-
-## Declaration
-
-```kotlin
-fun Button(title: String, action: () -> Unit): View
-```
-
-## Parameters
-
-| Name | Type | Description |
-|---|---|---|
-| `ACTION_ID` | `Int` | Bound action id |
-| `ENABLED` | `Bool` | Whether the button is interactive |
-| `LABEL` | `String` | Accessible name |
-
-## Availability
-
-Web · GTK · Qt

-# Color
-
-A solid-color, layout-greedy fill.
-
-## Overview
-
-A Color is a view, not a modifier. It expands to fill the space offered by its parent, which makes it useful as a background, separator, or colored accent block.

-## Live example
-

-Color(Color.token("color.primary"))
-                .frame(width = 160f, height = 56f)
-```

-

-fun Color(color: dev.pathland.view.core.Color): View
-```

-Design tokens adapt to the active light/dark scheme.

-                Icon(IconName.HOME)

-                Icon(IconName.HEART)
-                Icon(IconName.STAR)
-            }
-```

-## Declaration
-

-## Examples

-
-Icons inherit text metrics and keep a consistent visual weight.

-
-# MediaController
-
-A non-visual state object that owns media playback.
-
-## Overview
-
-MediaController is not a view. It owns the resource, playback state, position, volume, mute, loop, and rate as signals. Video surfaces reference it; audio has no view and is driven by your own controls.
-
-## Declaration
-
-```kotlin
-class MediaController(source: String) { ... }
-```
-
-## Parameters
-
-| Name | Type | Description |
-|---|---|---|
-| `MEDIA_SOURCE` | `String` | Asset reference |
-| `PLAYBACK_STATE` | `Bool` | Playing or paused |
-| `MEDIA_POSITION` | `Float` | Position in seconds |
-| `MEDIA_VOLUME` | `Float` | Volume 0..1 |
-| `MEDIA_MUTED` | `Bool` | Mute |
-| `MEDIA_LOOP` | `Bool` | Loop on end |
-| `MEDIA_RATE` | `Float` | Playback rate |
-
-## Availability
-
-Web · GTK · Qt
-
-## Notes
-- Call `attach()` once, outside any conditional branch, so playback is not recreated.
-- The controller's node is pinned; a layout swap does not restart playback.
-
-## See Also
-- [Video](video.md)

-
-# Getting started
-
-## Prerequisites
-
-- JDK 17 or newer
-- Maven 3.9+
-- (Optional) Rust for the native renderers
-
-## Build the JVM libraries
-
-```bash
-cd lib/java
-mvn install
-```
-
-The JVM path is pure Java/Kotlin: the HTML renderer and the inline Markdown
-parser are ports, so no Rust toolchain is required for the server demos.
-
-## Run the docs site
-
-```bash
-cd lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
-mvn quarkus:dev
-```
-
-Open `http://localhost:8080`. The marketing page is at `/` and this
-documentation starts at `/docs`.
-
-## How a page is loaded
-
-1. `DocsRepository` reads `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`, generated at build time from `src/main/resources/docs/**/*.md`.
-2. Each listed `.md` resource is parsed for front matter and a CommonMark body.
-3. `DocsLayout` renders the page, sidebar, TOC, and prev/next links.
-4. `Markdown(...)` maps blocks to Kotlin DSL views.
-5. The engine emits opcodes; the Quarkus starter renders SSR HTML and then
-   keeps the page live over `/_pathland/ws`.
-
-## Front matter
-
-```markdown
----
-title: Getting started
-description: Build the Java libraries and run the docs site locally.
-section: Start here
-order: 10
----
-```
-
-| Field | Purpose |
-|---|---|
-| `title` | Page heading and navigation label |
-| `description` | Head meta description and intro paragraph |
-| `section` | Sidebar group |
-| `order` | Sort order inside the section |
-| `route` | Optional override for the derived route |
-| `draft` | Hide the page |

-
-# Pathland documentation
-
-Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol. You describe **what**
-the UI is with a retained, declarative view tree; the engine emits a fixed
-16-byte opcode stream, and each renderer maps that stream onto its own native
-elements.
-
-> Write once, render anywhere — without a canvas and without a WebView.
-
-## What you get
-
-- A **binary protocol**: every instruction is exactly 16 bytes.
-- A **diff-based reactive engine**: only changed nodes emit opcodes.
-- **Native elements** on every target: GTK4, DOM, Qt Quick, and future hosts.
-- A **Kotlin DSL** with SwiftUI-shaped builders, signals, state, routing, and
-  media controllers.
-
-## Where to go next
-
-- [Component reference](components/index.md) — SwiftUI-style pages with live previews.
-- [Modifiers](modifiers/index.md) — the core padding, frame, style, and behavior modifiers.
-- [Getting started](getting-started.md) — build and run the Quarkus docs demo.
-- [Architecture](architecture.md) — opcodes, rings, arenas, and renderers.
-- [Kotlin DSL](kotlin-dsl.md) — components, modifiers, state, and routing.
-- [Markdown in the docs kit](markdown.md) — what the block renderer supports.
-
-## A first view
-
-```kotlin live=docs-first-view
-VStack(spacing = 12f) {
-    Text("Hello, Pathland")
-        .font(Font.largeTitle())
-    Button("Read the docs") {}
-        .buttonStyle(plainButtonStyle())
-        .navigate("/docs/getting-started")
-}
-```
-
-The same `View` tree can be mounted by a Quarkus server, a Spring Boot server,
-or a desktop host. The renderer is the only platform-specific part.

-title: Kotlin DSL
-description: Build views, state, routing, and navigation with the Kotlin authoring DSL.

----
-
-# Kotlin DSL
-
-The Kotlin DSL is the sole JVM authoring surface. It is shared by Quarkus,
-Spring Boot, and desktop hosts.
-
-## Components
-
-```kotlin
-VStack(spacing = 12f) {
-    Text("Hello")
-    HStack(spacing = 8f) {
-        Button("Save") { save() }
-        Button("Cancel") { cancel() }
-    }
-}
-```
-
-Common builders include `Text`, `Image`, `Button`, `TextField`, `VStack`,
-`HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `Spacer`, `Divider`, `Video`, and
-`NavigationStack`.
-
-## Modifiers
-
-```kotlin
-Text("Pathland")
-    .font(Font.title())
-    .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
-    .foregroundStyle(Color.token("color.primary"))
-    .padding(16f)
-    .background(Color.token("color.surface"))
-    .border(Color.token("color.border"), 1f, 8f)
-```
-
-Modifiers are chainable Kotlin values. Design-token references resolve in the
-renderer and adapt to light/dark schemes.
-
-## State and signals
-
-```kotlin
-class Counter : Component() {
-    private var count by state(0)
-
-    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 12f) {
-        Text("Count: $count")
-        Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
-    }
-}
-```
-
-A signal read in `body()` subscribes the component. A write re-renders only that
-component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound to a node stays
-fine-grained and does not re-run `body()`.
-
-## Routing
-
-```kotlin
-val router = navigator("/") {
-    route("/", HomeView())
-    route("/docs", DocsView())
-    fallback(NotFoundView())
-}
-
-NavigationStack(router)
-```
-
-Navigation intents are resolved by the emitter. Use `navigate` to replace the
-current route, or `push`/`pop` for a drill-down stack.
-
-## Markdown pages
-
-The docs kit adds `Markdown(...)`, `DocsLayout`, and `DocsRepository` on top of
-the DSL. Markdown is parsed into views — not into HTML.

----
-title: Markdown support
-description: The blocks the docs kit renders, and how they map to the Kotlin DSL.
-section: Guides

----
-
-# Markdown support
-
-The docs kit parses Markdown with commonmark-java plus GFM tables. It maps the
-AST to Kotlin DSL views; it never renders HTML directly.
-
-## Supported blocks
-
-| Block | DSL mapping |
-|---|---|
-| Heading | `Text` + heading `Font` + anchor id |
-| Paragraph | `Text` with inline runs |
-| Bullet list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `•` markers |
-| Ordered list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `1.`, `2.`, … |
-| Fenced code | monospace `CodeBlock` with preserved whitespace |
-| Block quote | accent bar + nested blocks |
-| Thematic break | `Divider` |
-| Table | `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling |
-| Image | `Image` with alt text |
-| Inline link | `AttributedString` link run |
-| Raw HTML | escaped literal text (never executed) |
-
-## Inline styles
-
-- **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~
-- [links](getting-started.md)
-- nested emphasis such as **bold with *italic* inside**
-
-## Images
-
-![The rendered browser demo](/docs-assets/screenshot_browser.png)
-
-Relative image paths are prefixed with `MarkdownOptions.imageBase`; absolute
-paths and URLs are left unchanged.
-
-## Code blocks
-
-```kotlin
-fun greeting(name: String): String = "Hello, $name"
-```
-
-Code blocks are monospace in v1. Syntax highlighting is tracked as
-[issue #188](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/188) because code is
-the primary content of a protocol docs site; the `AttributedString` model and
-renderers already support color runs.
-
-## Live examples
-
-Append `live=<id>` to a code fence to render the code and a registered live
-preview directly beneath it:
-
-````markdown
-```kotlin live=text-basic
-Text("Hello, Pathland").font(Font.title())
-```
-````
-
-The view for `text-basic` comes from the host's `MarkdownOptions.liveExamples`
-registry (`LiveExamples.byId` in this site). The docs never compile Markdown at
-runtime; every live id is checked by a test.
-

-title: Modifiers

----
-
-# Modifiers
-
-Modifiers are chainable values that describe a view's constraints and style. They
-emit `PARAMETER` opcodes and never compute layout: the native element decides
-how the constraints resolve.
-
-```kotlin
-Text("Hello")
-    .font(Font.title())
-    .foregroundStyle(Color.token("color.primary"))
-    .padding(16f)
-```
-
-## Core modifiers
-
-- [Padding](padding.md) — inset a view on all edges or per edge.
-- [Frame](frame.md) — fix, fill, or cap a view's width and height.
-- [Background](background.md) — paint a color behind a view.
-- [Border](border.md) — stroke an outline, optionally rounded.
-- [Corner radius](corner-radius.md) — round a view's corners.
-- [Shadow](shadow.md) — draw a drop shadow behind a view.
-- [Font](font.md) — choose typography, size, weight, and design.
-- [Foreground style](foreground-style.md) — tint text and glyphs.
-- [Line limit](line-limit.md) — cap the number of rendered lines.
-- [Opacity](opacity.md) — make a subtree translucent.
-- [White space](white-space.md) — choose how whitespace is preserved.
-- [Anchor](anchor.md) — assign a stable in-page anchor id.
-- [Disabled](disabled.md) — mark a control as non-interactive.
-- [Accessibility label](accessibility-label.md) — provide an accessible name.
-- [On tap gesture](on-tap-gesture.md) — handle a tap on any view.

-# pathland-docs-demo — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 7, 2026
-
-A Quarkus marketing + documentation site authored in the Kotlin DSL. Marketing
-lives at `/`; docs pages come from `.md` resources and render through
-`pathland-docs`. SSR + live deltas use the standard `pathland-quarkus` extension.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **Marketing page** at `/`: hero, screenshots, feature grid, a live
-  signal-bound playground, component/modifier CTAs, footer, window metadata.
-- **Docs site** at `/docs/...`: `DocsRepository` from the build-generated
-  `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`, sidebar/TOC/prev-next, per-page title and
-  description, canonical/OG/Twitter metadata through `PathlandApp.pageMetadata`.
-- **All content is Markdown**: getting started, architecture, Kotlin DSL,
-  Markdown support, `/docs/components/*` (one `.md` per component), and
-  `/docs/modifiers/*` (one `.md` per core modifier); screenshots served from
-  `/docs-assets/`.
-- **Live examples**: `LiveExamples.byId` registers the `live=<id>` preview views;
-  docs tests assert every live fence has an entry.
-- **Build-time index**: Maven Ant `fileset`/`pathconvert` scans
-  `src/main/resources/docs/**/*.md` into `target/classes/META-INF/pathland-docs.index`.
-- **Sitemap**: `PathlandApp.sitemapRoutes()` includes the docs pages.
-- **Router binding**: the per-session root binds the router to
-  `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`, so deep links render the right page on the first paint.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- Search (deferred).
-- A content watcher / live reload while editing Markdown.
-- Docs versioning and multi-project mounts.

-# pathland-docs — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 7, 2026
-
-The reusable Kotlin docs kit: CommonMark/GFM block parsing into Pathland views,
-code blocks, tables, a `.md` resource repository, and a docs page shell. It emits
-**views**, never HTML — the renderers remain the only HTML producers.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **Block Markdown** (`Markdown(...)`, CommonMark + GFM tables/strikethrough):
-  headings (with `ANCHOR` ids), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/nested lists, task
-  list markers, fenced/indented code blocks, block quotes, thematic breaks,
-  GFM tables, block images, inline links, and raw-HTML-as-literal-text.
-- **Inline rendering** into `AttributedString` (bold/italic/code/strikethrough/
-  links; images become alt text), with a `linkResolver` hook and `imageBase`
-  prefix.
-- **`CodeBlock`**: monospace, `WHITE_SPACE = PRE`, optional language label,
-  padding/background/border, horizontal scroll. **No syntax highlighting** (see
-  issue #188; deferred deliberately).
-- **Tables**: `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling and per-cell alignment.
-  Visual only — semantic table roles are deferred with the protocol work.
-- **TOC**: `MarkdownHeadings.extract` + `Slugger` (duplicate-safe ids).
-- **Link resolution**: `DocsRepository.resolveLink` maps relative `.md` targets
-  (including fragments/queries) to the target page's route; absolute URLs and
-  fragments pass through.
-- **`DocsPage.fromMarkdown`**: flat front matter (`title`, `description`,
-  `section`, `order`, `route`, `draft`, `updated`, `image`), route derivation,
-  and a `DocsRepository` that loads an index + classpath resources or a
-  filesystem directory.
-- **Live examples**: a ` ```kotlin live=<id> ` fence renders the code block and a
-  registered `MarkdownOptions.liveExamples` view directly beneath it; unknown
-  ids fall back to code-only.
-- **`DocsLayout`**: header, sidebar, content, TOC, prev/next, per-page
-  `windowMetadata`, plus optional `tocOverride`/content lambdas for structured
-  (non-Markdown) pages and a `liveExamples` registry.
-- **Tests**: `MarkdownViewTest` covers headings/anchors, lists/images, code
-  whitespace, GFM tables, front matter/routes, slug dedupe, raw HTML, and live
-  fences.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- Syntax highlighting (issue #188).
-- Semantic table roles (deferred; tables are visual grids for now).
-- Inline images inside a paragraph (rendered as alt text; block images only).
-- Footnotes, GFM alerts/admonitions, and autolinks beyond CommonMark.
-- A docs content watcher / live reload (the demo generates its index at build time;
-  `DocsRepository.fromDirectory` covers dev/tests).

 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
 their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
 `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
 `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
 capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
 - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
   Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
   application config (including
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
 
-- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.  # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** November 6, 2026
+**Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
 port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
 self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
 one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
 is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
 library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
   `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
   `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
   self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
   former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
+- **Layout parity with the Rust renderer**: `SCROLL_AXIS`-aware ScrollView
+  greed, finite `MAX_*` cap/bounded-fill semantics (no unbounded propagation or
+  cross-axis stretch), parent `ALIGNMENT` positioning, and the DOM hydration
+  `data-pathland-scroll-axis` attribute. The retired `IDEAL_*` properties are
+  ignored.
 - **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
   committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
   fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
   client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
 - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root,
   meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter
   cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
   Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The
   document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's
   `document_meta.document.html` fixture.
-- **Docs primitives**: `WHITE_SPACE` renders `white-space:normal|nowrap|pre|pre-wrap`; `ANCHOR` (STRING) becomes the element `id` attribute. Mirrored by the Rust renderer + DOM client.
 - **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
   (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
   attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
   surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
   size-that-fits snapshots.
 - **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
   the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
   default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
   `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
   `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
 - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
   with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
 - **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
   canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
   so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
 - **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
   `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
   external/webfont requests.
 - The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
   truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
   and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
 DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
 run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

 # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
   lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
   `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
   correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
   configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
   config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
-- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. The sitemap includes the app root plus every route declared by `PathlandApp.sitemapRoutes()` (e.g. docs pages).
+- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
   URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.

 # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
 signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
 interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
 Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
 Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.
 
 ## Implemented
 
-- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`
-  (incl. `WHITE_SPACE` 0x0022 and `ANCHOR` 0x201C), `Commands` (incl.
-  `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`,
-  `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.
+- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
+  `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`,
+  `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.
 - **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin
   model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and
   payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal<AttributedString>)`
   emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks.
-- **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the inline subset by
-  default (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``,
+- **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the v1 subset by default
+  (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``,
   `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`); `markdown = false` renders literal text.
-  `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now backed by **commonmark-java** (the
-  same parser the docs kit uses) in a restricted inline-only mode: only
-  paragraph blocks are accepted, so headings/lists/fences stay literal in a
-  text view. The existing Rust/JVM inline output contract is preserved by the
-  `MarkdownTest` parity suite. Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path;
-  rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive
-  `Text(Signal<String>)` parses on change.
+  `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now a **pure-Java parser** (no native
+  library, so it runs on every platform and under GraalVM native-image); it is a
+  behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-markdown` crate (pre-scan + bounded
+  cache). The Rust crate remains the parser for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts.
+  Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path; rich results emit
+  `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive `Text(Signal<String>)` parses on change.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
   `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
   **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled
   `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them
   against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are
   bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). A declared `opcodeCount` that overflows
   `Int` arithmetic now throws instead of triggering an OOM allocation.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
   `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
   protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
   `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
   public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
   Java source is generated.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
   protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
   the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
-- **Docs primitives**: `.whiteSpace(WhiteSpace.NORMAL|NO_WRAP|PRE|PRE_WRAP)` /
-  `.preserveWhitespace(wrap = false)` and `.anchor(id)` (a stable HTML/Native
-  anchor for deep links and TOCs).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module: `core`/`engine`/`dsl` are logical
   subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
   (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
   them into separate artifacts would require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on this module. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 # pathland-core — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **protocol core**: 16-byte opcode, SPSC ring buffers (both directions),
 bump arenas (both directions), memory layout, typed events, and the golden
 conformance vectors. The protocol contract is defined in `spec/`; this file
 tracks what this crate implements.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window/surface metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` 0x08, draft): an extensible field family (`TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCALE`) for the hosting window/surface, plus the shared no_std `WindowMeta` decoder helper. Spec + conformance vectors 44–45.
 
 - **Component types** (`constants.rs::component_type`): the full grouped map —
   `TEXT 0x01, IMAGE 0x02, COLOR 0x03, SHAPE 0x04, DIVIDER 0x05, SPACER 0x06,
   PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07, GAUGE 0x08, VIDEO 0x0A, ICON 0x0B, VSTACK 0x10, HSTACK 0x11, ZSTACK 0x12, GRID
 0x13, SCROLLVIEW 0x14, LAZY_VGRID 0x15, LAZY_HGRID 0x16, LAZY_VSTACK 0x1B,
    LAZY_HSTACK 0x1C, GRID_ROW 0x1D, PROXY_VIEW 0x1E, BUTTON 0x20, TEXT_FIELD 0x21, TEXT_EDITOR 0x22, TOGGLE
    0x24, SLIDER 0x25, STEPPER 0x26, DATE_PICKER 0x27, PICKER 0x28, MENU 0x29,
    COLOR_PICKER 0x2A, MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30, COMMENT 0x7F`. (`0x09` formerly
    `AUDIO` is freed — audio has no view; spec/MEDIA.md.)
 - **Media kit** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (`0x30`, **non-visual**,
   layout-transparent) owns the resource + transport; a `VIDEO` (`0x0A`) surface
   references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (`0x103A`). Transport properties
   `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035), `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036), `MEDIA_VOLUME` (0x1037),
   `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D),
   `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E); the `MEDIA_*` events target the **controller** id and add
   `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` (0x14). Covered by conformance vectors 39–41.
 - **`PROXY_VIEW`** (`0x1E`) — a container whose child subtree is served by another
   Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md); the id is the only wire-visible part of the
   proxy contract (the origin subtree's nodes are ordinary opcodes with
   **id-remapped** node ids). Covered by conformance vector 38.
 - **`GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`** (`0x001E`/`0x001F`, F32) track-count properties
   for grids (positive = count, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit; never a pixel box),
   **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track specs (takes precedence over the
   counts), and the **`GRID_ROW`** (`0x1D`) component (a grid child whose children
   are one row's cells) — all covered by conformance vectors (34–36).
 - **`ALIGNMENT` (0x0002) is a 2D position code (0–8)**: `0` topLeading, `1`
   center, `2` bottomTrailing, `3` topCenter, `4` bottomCenter, `5` centerLeading,
   `6` centerTrailing, `7` topTrailing, `8` bottomLeading. Stacks read one axis
   (`VSTACK`→horizontal, `HSTACK`→vertical; codes 0/1/2 backward-compatible);
   `ZSTACK`/grids read both. Position-only — stretching is a child's `FILL`
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, never an alignment (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). Covered by
   conformance vector 37 (`ALIGNMENT` topCenter = 3).
 - **Properties** (`property_id`): the full `spec/MODIFIERS.md` catalog —
   stack/text/styling/semantic IDs plus every draft modifier (`SHAPE_KIND`,
   layout `OFFSET`/`POSITION`/frame bounds/`FIXED_SIZE`/`LAYOUT_PRIORITY`/
   `ASPECT_RATIO`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`, text-format
   `FONT_STYLE`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`FONT_WIDTH`/`KERNING`/`TRACKING`/
   `BASELINE_OFFSET`/`LINE_SPACING`/`TEXT_CASE`/`UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
   effects `SHADOW_*`/`BLUR_RADIUS`/`SATURATION`/`CONTRAST`/`BRIGHTNESS`/
   `GRAYSCALE`/`HUE_ROTATION`/`COLOR_MULTIPLY`/`COLOR_INVERT`,
   `ROTATION_DEGREES`/`SCALE`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, control drafts
   `STEP_VALUE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`IS_SECURE`/`PROGRESS`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`/
   `SELECTION`/`COLOR_VALUE`/`DATE_PICKER_MODE`/`PICKER_STYLE`,
   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`, the **asset references** `IMAGE_SOURCE`
   and `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B) — STRING asset refs (URL /
   resource / path), never embedded in the opcode stream (`AUDIO` 0x09 and
   `AUDIO_SOURCE` 0x1033 / `VIDEO_SOURCE` 0x1034 are freed — audio has no view,
   spec/MEDIA.md); `ICON_NAME` (0x1038,
   STRING — the `ICON` primitive's canonical name, spec/ICONS.md); plus the navigation
   drafts `TRANSITION` (0x1031), `ROUTE` (0x2019, STRING), `NAV_DEPTH` (0x201A,
   U32 — the `NavigationContainer`'s back-stack depth, so native navigation
   adapters reconcile their page stack by depth) and `NAV_CHROME` (0x201B,
   F32-enum chrome mode: `PlatformDefault`=0 / `Custom`=1 — the renderer
   supplies default navigation chrome, or the developer owns all nav UI)).
 - **`ICON` vocabulary** (`constants::icon`): the canonical `ICON_NAME` names
   (spec/ICONS.md) as `&str` consts + `NAMES` + `is_canonical` — the protocol
   vocabulary only; the canonical-name → native-glyph mapping is renderer-owned
   (GTK + web each define their own).
 - **Attributed text** (`PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`, `0x05`) +
   `AttributedString` model/codec: text + UTF-8-byte range style runs (v1:
   `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`COLOR`/`FONT_STYLE`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`UNDERLINE`/
   `STRIKETHROUGH`) + links, arena payload encode/decode, `Guest::set_attributed_text`,
   and overlap-resolving `segments()`. Covered by conformance vector 46.
 - **Commands**: `TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move (append = `u32::MAX`);
   `PARAMETER` `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`/`SET_TEXT`/`SET_DATE`/
   `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`; `META`
   `RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT`/`RESYNC`. **`META::PING`/`PONG`** (0x04/0x05) are the
   transport-liveness heartbeat — **network batch transport only** (a shared-memory
   ring consumer MUST NOT emit/expect/relay them); the core engine never produces
   them. `META::ENVIRONMENT` is the extensible
   platform-environment field family (`environment::VIEWPORT_WIDTH`/
   `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT`/`ROUTE` — the `ROUTE` string uses the `TEXT_CHANGED`/
   `NAVIGATE` dual convention).
 - **Typed `Event` enum**: pointer/key/value/text events (0x01–0x07) plus the
   draft `FocusChanged`, `EditingChanged`, `Submit`, `Scroll`, `Wheel`,
   `DateChanged` (0x08–0x0D) and `Navigate` (0x0E) — all encode/decode
   round-trip. `Navigate { url: Some(_) }` resolves its URL from the event arena
   / batch string section (same dual convention as `TEXT_CHANGED`);
   `Navigate { url: None }` is a native back request (decodes from a bare
   opcode).
 - **`Guest::set_date`** helper (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`).
 - **`Guest::set_design_token`** helper (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`): global token
   override (`path` arena string, `valueType`, `value`), incl. `dark.`-prefixed
   dark variants (spec/TOKENS.md).
 - **`Guest::set_design_token_string`** helper: STRING-valued token override —
   both the path and the value ride the arena (`A` = path ref, `B` = STRING,
   `C` = value ref).
 - **`Guest::set_color_scheme` / `Guest::reset_theme`** helpers
   (`META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` / `META::RESET_THEME`): force the renderer color
   scheme (platform/light/dark) and clear all application token overrides.
 - **`pathland_core::tokens`** — the **reference resolution algorithm**
   (spec/TOKENS.md): `dark.*` layer → override → default → parent-fallback →
   fallback, the generative `space.<N>` family (`space.base` × N), and the
   `TokenValue`/`Scheme`/`TokenTables` types. Pure `no_std` + `alloc`;
   renderers keep their own tables and call `tokens::resolve`. `resolve_ref`
   implements explicit `dark.` references (forced dark layer regardless of the
   active scheme). `TIER1_TOKENS` is the canonical Tier-1 catalog used by the
   renderer default-table coverage tests. The full "Design-Token Resolution
   Conformance" table (spec/CONFORMANCE.md) is tested here.
 - **`value_type_for`** matches `spec/MODIFIERS.md`'s canonical mapping
   (COLOR / U32 / U8 / STRING / F32-enum-code / LIST); the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value
   type (`0x08`) is available per-instance on `SET_PROPERTY`. **`LIST`** (`0x09`)
   is the arena-backed array value type (a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
 - **`SizeThatFits`** (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` `0x17`, `FIT_QUERY` `0x1039` LIST,
   `FIT_CHANGED` `0x13`): the fit slot shows its single selected child (only it
   is transmitted); `fit::fit_index` implements the spec'd pick (largest
   threshold the width meets, ascending + stable, index 0 fallback) shared by
   every renderer.
 - **Listener bits**: 0–9 (`POINTER_*`, `KEY_*`, `FOCUS`, `EDITING`, `SUBMIT`,

   typographies** (spec/MODIFIERS.md): `LARGE_TITLE`…`HEADLINE` (heading styles →

   `CAPTION`/`CAPTION2` (plain `<span>` text). `TEXT_STYLE = 0x1032`.

   ring, guest arena, host→guest **event arena** (two-way string section — a
   host `send_event(TextChanged)` round-trips text over the shared ring).

   the read cursor numerically (the producer wraps through 0), and the naive
   `write < read` guard in `read_events` / `Host::frames` **permanently
   deadlocked the ring** at the wrap boundary — the reader never advanced again,
   the writer sat "full", and every subsequent drain returned empty (the GTK
   demo's "UI freezes some time into a song, audio keeps playing": events were
   written but `drain_events` returned 0 forever). Both readers now count the
   pending run modulo the ring size and drain across the wrap in ring order
   (`Host::frames` drains the wrapped head in one call and the tail in the next,
   preserving opcode order). Event drains also take a `max` bound
   (`drain_event_opcodes_max`) so a fixed-size C buffer never drops events it
   could not copy. Regression tests: `ring::tests::read_events_drains_a_wrapped_producer`
   + `tests::host_frames_survives_a_wrapped_write_cursor`.

   bytes **incl. vectors 17–18, 20–27** (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (COLOR +
   STRING-valued), `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY`, `NAVIGATE`±URL,
   `ROUTE`, `TRANSITION`, `META::ENVIRONMENT` VIEWPORT_WIDTH + ROUTE), vectors
   **34–38** (grid `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`/`GRID_TRACKS`, `GRID_ROW`,
   `ALIGNMENT` topCenter, `PROXY_VIEW`), and the network-only **`META::PING`/`PONG`** heartbeat
   opcodes; a ring
   test proving `Guest::set_design_token` emits vector 17 byte-exactly;
   `cargo test` enforces them.

   codec over the shared ring** (event-arena absolute offset for a `ROUTE`
   field) and a native emitter are not wired yet — the web path encodes/decodes
   it in the TS client + Java `FrameCodec` (batch string section).

   no named value constants. (`ROLE` and `TEXT_STYLE` are now the canonical
   exceptions — see `constants::role` / `constants::text_style` above; the
   remaining enum codes live in the specs + the `pathland-ts-codegen` enum
   table.)
 - No **general STRING-property diff path** in `pathland-engine` (the engine
   stores numeric properties + design-token refs only). `ROUTE` (STRING) will
   need a small string-property capability when the Rust router lands (Phase 3);
   `TRANSITION` (F32) is handled by the generic property diff today.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-core` — conformance vectors, opcode round-trips,
 arena, ring, event-ring (incl. shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` + `Navigate` round
 trips and `META::RESET` event-arena recycle), `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` /
 `META::RESET_THEME` vectors, the token resolution table (incl. explicit `dark.`
 refs), randomized tests.

No overrides → no extra element. - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the renderer. - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`, the **shared control core** (`--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*`), and the component tokens (`--pl-toggle-*`, `--pl-slider-*`, `--pl-progress-*`, `--pl-gauge-*`, `--pl-stepper-*`, `--pl-picker-*`, `--pl-menu-*`, `--pl-label-*`, `--pl-size-control-*`), all with light + dark values. `.pathland-*` rules reference the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components. - **Forced scheme**: `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` sets `data-pathland-scheme` on `<html>`; the platform-dark media rule is scoped to `:root:not([data-pathland-scheme])` and the dark values are repeated under `:root[data-pathland-scheme="dark"]`.
